https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/a.summary: The major overhaul of Nigeria’s tax system by the federal government has started to yield fruits as just 20 firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) paid a whooping N3.04 trillion as income tax to Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) and other agencies in first half ended June 30, 2026. The firms cut across banking sector, cement manufacturing, Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG), telecommunication, among other sectors in Nigeria economy.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/a.summary_zh: 联邦政府对尼日利亚税收体系的重大改革已开始产生成果，在截至2026年6月30日的上半年，仅在尼日利亚交易所（NGX）上市的20家公司就向尼日利亚税务局（NRS）和其他机构缴纳了高达3.04万亿奈拉的所得税。这些公司涵盖银行部门、水泥制造、快速消费品（FMCG）、电信以及尼日利亚经济的其他部门。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/a.body: The major overhaul of Nigeria’s tax system by the federal government has started to yield fruits as just 20 firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) paid a whooping N3.04 trillion as income tax to Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) and other agencies in first half ended June 30, 2026. This represents an increase of 79.5 per cent from N1.69 trillion remitted in first half of 2025. The firms cut across banking sector, cement manufacturing, Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG), telecommunication, among other sectors in Nigeria economy. The standard corporate income tax rate remains 30 per cent, but the reforms by NRS introduced a 4 per cent development levy on assessable profits for companies within scope. This levy replaced several separate federal levies, so the net impact depends on what each company paid previously. Nigeria’s tax reforms, particularly the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and related legislation that took effect on January 1, 2026, have important implications for companies listed on the NGX. They affect corporate tax costs, cash flow, dividend capacity, investment decisions, compliance expenses and, potentially, share-price performance. But expert believe the impact will not be the same for every company. “It will depend on profitability, sector, tax incentives, capital expenditure, financing structure and how effectively each company adapts to the new rules,” said a tax expert. Meanwhile, analysis of the financial results of the 20 firms showed that Seplat Energy Plc, followed by Aradel Holdings paid the highest tax to revenue agencies in the period under review. Seplat Energy in the H1 2026 declared N564.94 billion tax expenses, a 37.2 per cent increase over N411.59 billion reported in H1 2025, while Aradel Holdings announced N561.7 billion tax expenses in H1 2026, up by 1150.4 per cent from N44.92billion in H1 2025. Seplat in a statement said, “In accordance with IAS 34: Interim Financial Reporting, income tax expense for the interim period has been determined using the estimated weighted average annual effective income tax rate expected for the full financial year. This estimate is reviewed at each interim reporting date and adjusted, where necessary, to reflect changes in the expected annual tax rate. “Income tax expense for the group is analysed by Oil segment – Half year ended N533.7 billion (H1 2025: N353.5 billion); 3 months ended N372.9 billion (H1 2025: N97.5 billion) and Gas Segment – Half year ended N31.2 billion (H1 2025: N58.1 billion); 3 months ended N15.4 billion (H1 2025: N34.8 billion). The company said it has applied the provisions of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which became effective in January 2026 and require Education Tax, the NASENI levy, and the Police Trust Fund Levy to be consolidated into Development Levy. In the period under review, MTN Nigeria Communications Plc declared N384.05billion tax income, which is 85 per cent increase over N207.41 billion in H1 2025. Dangote Cement announced N342.85 billion income tax expense in H1 2026, a growth of 63.6 per cent from N209.6billion reported in H1 2025. Of the N3.04 trillion income tax expense, a total of nine banks remitted N845.79 billion in H1 2026, about 42 per cent increase over N596.79 billion in H1 2025. Zenith Bank led eight others with the highest tax income in the period, announcing N206.84 billion, about 121.34 per cent increase over N93.45billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Following the 121.34 per cent increase in tax income, Zenith Bank saw its profit dropped by 19.06 per cent to N430.76 billion in H1 2026. Analysts expressed the importance of companies remitting taxes to government agencies, stressing that listing on the NGX gives room for companies to be transparent in tax payment to government agencies. Commenting, Vice-President, Highcap Securities Limited, Mr. David Adnori stated that listed companies may be paying more taxes this year, stressing on its importance on shareholders’ return.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/a.title_zh: 在税收改革中，20家蓝筹公司向NRS及其他机构汇出N3.04trn
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/a.body_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府对税收体系的重大改革已开始产生成果，在截至2026年6月30日的上半年，只有20家在尼日利亚交易所有限公司（NGX）上市的公司向尼日利亚税务局（NRS）和其他机构缴纳了高达3.04万亿奈拉的所得税。这比2025年上半年汇缴的1.69万亿奈拉增长了79.5%。这些公司涵盖银行业、水泥制造、快速消费品（FMCG）、电信以及尼日利亚经济的其他部门。标准公司所得税税率仍为30%，但NRS的改革对范围内的公司按应税利润引入了4%的发展税。该税取代了若干单独的联邦税费，因此净影响取决于每家公司此前缴纳的金额。尼日利亚的税收改革，特别是2025年尼日利亚税收法及相关立法于2026年1月1日生效，对在NGX上市的公司具有重要影响。它们影响公司税负、现金流、派息能力、投资决策、合规费用，并可能影响股价表现。但专家认为，对每家公司的影响不会相同。“这将取决于盈利能力、行业、税收激励、资本支出、融资结构以及每家公司适应新规则的效率，”一位税务专家表示。与此同时，对这20家公司财务结果的分析显示，Seplat Energy Plc其次是Aradel Holdings在审查期间向税务机构缴纳了最高税款。Seplat Energy在2026年上半年申报了5649.4亿奈拉的税费支出，比2025年上半年报告的4115.9亿奈拉增长37.2%，而Aradel Holdings在2026年上半年宣布了5617亿奈拉的税费支出，比2025年上半年的449.2亿奈拉增长1150.4%。Seplat在一份声明中表示，“根据IAS 34：中期财务报告，中期所得税费用已使用预计适用于整个财政年度的加权平均年度有效所得税税率确定。该估计在每个中期报告日进行审查，并在必要时进行调整，以反映预期年度税率的变化。“集团的所得税费用按石油板块分析——半年结束为5337亿奈拉（2025年上半年：3535亿奈拉）；3个月结束为3729亿奈拉（2025年上半年：975亿奈拉）和天然气板块——半年结束为312亿奈拉（2025年上半年：581亿奈拉）；3个月结束为154亿奈拉（2025年上半年：348亿奈拉）。该公司表示，它已适用2025年尼日利亚税收法的规定，该法于2026年1月生效，要求将教育税、NASENI税和警察信托基金税合并为发展税。在审查期间，MTN Nigeria Communications Plc申报了3840.5亿奈拉的所得税收入，比2025年上半年的2074.1亿奈拉增长85%。Dangote Cement在2026年上半年宣布了3428.5亿奈拉的所得税费用，比2025年上半年报告的2096亿奈拉增长63.6%。在3.04万亿奈拉的所得税费用中，共有九家银行在2026年上半年汇缴了8457.9亿奈拉，较2025年上半年的5967.9亿奈拉增长约42%。Zenith Bank在该期间领先其他八家，宣布了2068.4亿奈拉的最高所得税收入，较2025年同期934.5亿奈拉增长约121.34%。在所得税收入增长121.34%之后，Zenith Bank的利润在2026年上半年下降19.06%至4307.6亿奈拉。分析师强调了公司向政府机构缴纳税款的重要性，强调在NGX上市使公司能够透明地向政府机构缴纳税款。在评论中，Highcap Securities Limited副总裁David Adnori先生表示，上市公司今年可能缴纳更多税款，并强调这对股东回报的重要性。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/t.title: Towards Building Healthy Economy
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/t.summary: The objectives of the economic reforms by the federal government and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) are primarily to correct the anomalies, and towards building a healthy and sustainable economy going forward, though the policy implementations may be disruptive and distressful for a period in the timeline, but as it is said, “no pain, no gain”.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/t.summary_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府和尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）经济改革的目标主要是纠正异常现象，并朝着建设一个健康和可持续的经济迈进，尽管政策实施可能会在一段时间内具有破坏性和带来压力，但正如人们所说，“没有付出，就没有收获”。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/t.body: The objectives of the economic reforms by the federal government and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) are primarily to correct the anomalies, and towards building a healthy and sustainable economy going forward, though the policy implementations may be disruptive and distressful for a period in the timeline, but as it is said, “no pain, no gain”. Economy is the focal point and lifeblood of the people and which is why responsible governments and all relevant institutions would do all necessary things to ensure a healthy and sustainable economy. Because of the inevitable disruptive effects of the economic reforms, President Tinubu has thus far introduced some social safety nets to help cushion the impact of the reforms towards building a healthy economy in the long run. Basically, a healthy economy features a robust financial system, low inflation, stable prices, low unemployment/ high employment (so that those who want jobs can easily find one), and wages that match or beat inflation. Other features are moderate interest rate to channel capital to productive sectors, stable exchange rate to enable businesses plan with certainty, high consumer confidence, balanced imports and exports and growth in GDP. CBN has thus far implemented some notable policies that have positively impacted some of the above-listed economic variables as part of the reforms towards building a healthy economy. The apex bank keyed into the envisioned US$1trillion economy envisioned by President Tinubu and has implemented a proactive and seamless banks recapitalisation policy to ensure a robust financial system. It is expected that the recapitalised banks will channel credits into productive sectors especially agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure, technology and small and medium enterprises to justify the essence of their recapitalisation. After the recapitalisation, CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso noted that the apex bank had shifted focus to ensuring that stronger capital translated into support for productive activities. CBN has also stabilized the exchange rate and fought inflation aggressively and reduced it from it previous high levels to 15.39% and is still targeting to moderate it further. With the reforms, Nigeria’s economy presently can be likened to a sick patient that was taken to the intensive care unit of a hospital and underwent two major life-saving surgeries for stabilization and subsequent healing and expected restoration of good health. The unified exchange rate has its pros and cons but CBN’s target goals for adopting the new regime are to remove the ambiguities of the previous exchange rate regime and ensure transparency, true price discovery through “willing buyer, willing seller” mechanism, curb rent-seeking and to attract foreign direct investments (FDIs). The unified exchange rate has contributed in stabilizing the economy. The fuel subsidy removal was an inevitable, bold and courageous policy action because fuel subsidy constituted a huge financial burden and drained government resources which often led to large deficits. It also led to fuel smuggling and scarcity and corruption. The removal of fuel subsidy was a financial lifeline for the economy. It generated about N 15.8 trillion to the economy between June 2023 and December 2025. World bank noted that between 2020 and 2021, inflation left about eight million more Nigerians below the poverty line and increased the number of poor people to about 90 million. To minimize poverty and actualize the objective and drive of the present economic reform towards building a healthy economy, the present macroeconomic stability should be maintained and inflation should be further moderated through a combination of the monetarist policy by CBN and the boosting of the supply side of the economy.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/t.title_zh: 朝着建设健康经济迈进
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/t.body_zh: 联邦政府和尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）的经济改革目标主要是纠正异常现象，并朝着建设一个健康和可持续的经济体迈进，尽管政策实施可能会在一段时间内具有破坏性和带来痛苦，但正如俗语所说，“不劳无获”。经济是人民的焦点和命脉，这就是为什么负责任的政府和所有相关机构会尽一切必要努力来确保一个健康和可持续的经济。由于经济改革的不可避免的破坏性影响，总统蒂努布迄今引入了一些社会安全网，以帮助缓冲改革的影响，朝着长期建设健康经济迈进。基本上，健康的经济具有以下特征：强大的金融体系、低通胀、稳定的价格、低失业率/高就业率（这样那些想要工作的人可以轻松找到一份工作），以及与通胀相匹配或超过通胀的工资。其他特征包括适度的利率以将资本引导到生产部门、稳定的汇率以使企业能够确定地进行规划、高消费者信心、平衡的进出口以及GDP增长。CBN迄今实施了一些显著的政策，这些政策积极影响了上述部分经济变量，作为朝着建设健康经济进行改革的一部分。央行加入了总统蒂努布设想的1万亿美元经济愿景，并实施了积极且无缝的银行资本重组政策，以确保强大的金融体系。预计资本重组后的银行将把信贷引导到生产部门，特别是农业、制造业、基础设施、技术以及中小企业，以证明其资本重组的本质。在资本重组之后，CBN行长奥拉耶米·卡多索指出，央行已将重点转移到确保更强的资本转化为对生产活动的支持。CBN还稳定了汇率，并积极对抗通胀，将其从之前的高水平降低到15.39%，并且仍在目标进一步适度降低它。通过改革，尼日利亚经济目前可以比作一个被带到医院重症监护室的病人，接受了两次重大的挽救生命的 surgery 以实现稳定以及随后的愈合和预期恢复良好健康。统一的汇率有其利弊，但CBN采用新制度的目標目标是消除先前汇率制度的模糊性，并确保透明度，通过“愿意买方、愿意卖方”机制实现真实的价格发现，遏制寻租并吸引外国直接投资（FDIs）。统一的汇率有助于稳定经济。取消燃料补贴是一项不可避免的、大胆且勇敢的政策行动，因为燃料补贴构成了巨大的财政负担并耗尽了政府资源，这往往导致巨额赤字。它还导致燃料走私、短缺和腐败。取消燃料补贴是经济的金融生命线。它在2023年6月至2025年12月期间为经济带来了约15.8万亿奈拉。世界银行指出，在2020年至2021年期间，通胀使另外约800万尼日利亚人陷入贫困线以下，并将贫困人口数量增加到约9000万。为了最小化贫困并实现当前经济改革朝着建设健康经济的目标和动力，目前的宏观经济稳定应得到维持，并应通过CBN的货币主义政策与经济供给侧的提振相结合，进一步适度降低通胀。

The Commissioner for Insurance, Mr Olusegun Ayo Omosehin had at a press briefing in Lagos told the media that insurers would by the end of September receive their funds. Addressing newsmen in Lagos, the Chairman, Nigerian Insurers Association (NIA), Mrs. Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu, disclosed that NAICOM has instructed CBN to release the funds. She however assured operators that the funds were expected to be fully returned within this month of October. “NAICOM has done its part by issuing instructions to the CBN. The funds will be returned to the exact accounts from which they were sent once the CBN completes its verification,” she stated. She urged insurance operators that crossed the recapitalisation hurdle to deploy the enhanced capital base to expand local underwriting capacity, increase retention during reinsurance renewals, and provide cover for emerging exposures such as cyber and climate risks. She said having successfully concluded the recapitalisation exercise the regulator has come up with implementation of the Risk Base Capital model. She said the regulator has appointed global professional services firm Ernst & Young (EY) as its consultant to guide the Nigerian insurance industry through a transparent and structured transition to a Risk-Based Capital (RBC) regime. According to her, the Commissioner for Insurance, Olusegun Omosehin, announced the appointment during the insurers’ committee meeting alongside other crucial regulatory directives shaping the post-recapitalisation era. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/i.body_zh: 在最近的资本重组进程结束后，保险公司正急切等待其托管账户中的3000亿奈拉资金获释，因为尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）已开始尽职调查。最近，国家保险委员会（NAICOM）表示，它已正式指示央行释放资金。保险专员Olusegun Ayo Omosehin先生在拉各斯的一次新闻发布会上告诉媒体，保险公司将在9月底前收到他们的资金。在拉各斯向新闻界发表讲话时，尼日利亚保险公司协会（NIA）主席Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu女士透露，NAICOM已指示CBN释放资金。然而，她向经营者保证，这些资金预计将在本10月份内全部返还。“NAICOM已经完成了它的部分工作，即向CBN发出指示。一旦CBN完成其验证，资金将返还到发送它们的原始账户，”她表示。她敦促那些跨越了资本重组障碍的保险经营者，将增强的资本基础用于扩大本地承保能力，在再保险续约期间增加留存，并为网络和气候风险等新兴风险提供保障。她说，在成功完成资本重组工作后，监管机构已提出实施基于风险的资本模型。她说，监管机构已任命全球专业服务公司Ernst & Young（EY）作为其顾问，指导尼日利亚保险业通过透明和结构化的过渡进入基于风险的资本（RBC）制度。据她介绍，保险专员Olusegun Omosehin在保险公司委员会会议上宣布了这一任命，同时还有其他塑造资本重组后时代的关键监管指令。THISDAY成立于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都特区和世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术与有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真相和理性，涵盖从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列问题。您可以通过hello@thisdaylive.com与我们联系，或访问我们的联系页面。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/h.summary: The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA), has condemned the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, over what it described as a misplaced fixation on President Bola Tinubu’s second-term prospects while Nigerians endured crushing poverty, soaring petrol prices and an escalating cost-of-living crisis.

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/h.body: The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA), has condemned the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, over what it described as a misplaced fixation on President Bola Tinubu’s second-term prospects while Nigerians endured crushing poverty, soaring petrol prices and an escalating cost-of-living crisis. HURIWA, in a statement by its national coordinator, Emmanuel Onwubiko, said Oyedele should stop acting like a political promoter for the president and concentrate on the economic responsibilities for which he was appointed. The association observed that Nigerians needed urgent answers to their economic problems, not assurances about what international investors supposedly think of Tinubu’s chances in the 2027 election. HURIWA maintained that the minister’s suggestion that markets and the international community were already pricing in a Tinubu second term was, at best, his own assessment and could not be presented as a verdict on Nigeria’s political future. Onwubiko said the power to elect the country’s next president belonged to Nigerians, not foreign investors, global financial institutions or powerful boardroom interests. HURIWA observed that the Nigerian economy could not be defended with political projections while citizens were being battered by the consequences of policies they can barely survive. The association, therefore, challenged Oyedele to explain how the administration intended to make life bearable for workers whose wages have been overwhelmed by the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential needs. HURIWA added that the government must confront legitimate concerns about its growing reliance on borrowing. It observed that reports of increased revenue collections by government agencies should provoke questions about expenditure priorities, fiscal discipline and why borrowing remains a recurring feature of public finance. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/h.body_zh: 尼日利亚人权作家协会（HURIWA）谴责财政部长泰沃·奥耶德莱（Taiwo Oyedele），称其对总统博拉·蒂努布（Bola Tinubu）第二任期前景的关注 misplaced，而尼日利亚人正忍受着极度贫困、飙升的汽油价格以及不断升级的生活成本危机。HURIWA 在其全国协调员埃马纽埃尔·奥努比科（Emmanuel Onwubiko）发表的一份声明中表示，奥耶德莱应该停止像总统的政治推手那样行事，而应专注于他被任命的经济职责。该协会指出，尼日利亚人需要对其经济问题的紧急答案，而不是关于国际投资者 supposedly 如何看待蒂努布在2027年选举机会的保证。HURIWA 坚持认为，部长关于市场和国际社会已经在为蒂努布第二任期定价的说法充其量只是他自己的评估，不能作为对尼日利亚政治未来的判决。奥努比科表示，选举该国下一任总统的权力属于尼日利亚人，而不是外国投资者、全球金融机构或强大的董事会利益。HURIWA 指出，在公民被他们几乎无法生存的政策后果所打击之际，不能用政治预测来捍卫尼日利亚经济。因此，该协会要求奥耶德莱解释政府打算如何让工人们的生活变得可以忍受，他们的工资已被食品、交通、电力和其他基本需求成本所压倒。HURIWA 补充说，政府必须面对对其日益依赖借款的合理关切。它指出，政府机构收入征收增加的报告应该引发关于支出优先事项、财政纪律以及为什么借款仍然是公共财政反复出现特征的问题。THISDAY 成立于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都特区和世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术与有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真相和理性，涵盖从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列问题。您可以通过 hello@thisdaylive.com 给我们发邮件或访问我们的联系页面。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/eu-tariffs-a.summary_zh: 乌克兰最大钢铁公司之一的老板呼吁欧盟取消对该国生产的产品的进口限制，认为这些限制与旨在遏制来自中国等国的廉价进口的措施“捆绑在一起”。Metinvest首席执行官Yuriy Ryzhenkov告诉BBC，最近对进口到欧盟的钢铁征收的关税“不公平”，并且“在没有考虑乌克兰所处的情况的情况下”实施。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/eu-tariffs-a.body: The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies has called on the European Union to drop import restrictions on products made in the country, arguing that they have been "bundled together" with measures aimed at curbing cheap imports from the likes of China. Yuriy Ryzhenkov, chief executive of Metinvest, told the BBC the recently imposed tariffs on imported steel to the EU were "unfair" and had been put in place "without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in". He said he wished to see "at least a carve-out" for Ukraine to access the EU market. A spokesperson for the European Commission said the EU "took into account the difficult situation" of Ukraine when deciding its steel policy. The trading bloc has recently imposed restrictions on steel imports to protect steel manufacturers in member nations. It has capped the amount of steel which can enter the EU tax-free at 18.3 million tonnes per year - a 47% reduction from 2024 levels. There are some country-specific quotas in the policy, but the overall aim is to reduce the amount of steel that can be imported, as member nations struggle to compete with cheap imports from countries like China and Turkey. Despite a free trade agreement (FTA) between the EU and Ukraine, the FTA does not prevent the EU from introducing separate trade protection measures. "Ukraine has been bundled together into those measures without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in," Ryzhenkov said, pointing to the war with Russia. "Access to the European market is crucial for survival," he added. "The restrictive measures that have been put in place by the authorities in the European Union, they don't help. The Ukraine steel industry estimates steel exports to the EU could ultimately fall by about 50–60%. The EU said Ukraine's specific steel quota guaranteed exports of the metal, but acknowledged this was at a "level lower than in the past years". "Despite the war effort, Ukraine remains an important exporter of steel to the EU," a spokesperson said, adding it had "offered compensations" to its largest suppliers, which included Ukraine. Steel products are a foundation in Ukraine's economy. Before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, metallurgy and mining accounted for roughly 10% of Ukraine's national income and a third of its exports. The EU is its top customer. But the industry has suffered from the continued Russian bombardment. All of Ukraine's steel mills have been bombed at points since the conflict began in 2022, but Ryzhenkov said strikes had "intensified significantly recently". At one point in September, there was "no single tonne of steel produced" in Ukraine for the first time in about 150 years, he added. Almost 800 Metinvest workers have been killed since the war began. Ryzhenkov said the company had "improved the covered areas" at its mills where workers can shelter during air raids. "Unfortunately, you cannot cover a whole steel mill to avoid it being damaged." Ryzhenkov said he expected the coming winter to be "one of the hardest in our history"

https://www.myjoyonline.com/eu-tariffs-a.body_zh: 乌克兰最大钢铁公司之一的老板呼吁欧盟取消对该国生产的产品的进口限制，认为这些限制已被“捆绑在一起”，与旨在遏制来自中国等国的廉价进口的措施混为一谈。Metinvest首席执行官尤里·雷任科夫告诉BBC，最近对进口到欧盟的钢铁征收的关税“不公平”，并且“在没有考虑乌克兰所处情况的情况下”实施。他说，他希望看到“至少为乌克兰开辟一个例外”，以便进入欧盟市场。欧盟委员会发言人表示，欧盟在决定其钢铁政策时“考虑到了乌克兰的困难处境”。这个贸易集团最近对钢铁进口实施了限制，以保护成员国的钢铁制造商。它将可以免税进入欧盟的钢铁数量限制在每年1830万吨——比2024年的水平减少47%。该政策中有一些国家特定的配额，但总体目标是减少可以进口的钢铁数量，因为成员国难以与来自中国和土耳其等国的廉价进口竞争。尽管欧盟与乌克兰之间有自由贸易协定（FTA），但该FTA并不阻止欧盟引入单独的贸易保护措施。“乌克兰被捆绑到这些措施中，而没有考虑乌克兰所处的情况，”雷任科夫说，并指出了与俄罗斯的战争。“进入欧洲市场对生存至关重要，”他补充道。“欧盟当局实施的限制性措施，它们没有帮助。乌克兰钢铁行业估计，对欧盟的钢铁出口最终可能下降约50-60%。欧盟表示，乌克兰特定的钢铁配额保证了该金属的出口，但承认这处于‘低于过去几年的水平’。尽管有战争努力，乌克兰仍然是欧盟重要的钢铁出口国，”一位发言人说，并补充说它已“向其最大供应商提供补偿”，其中包括乌克兰。钢铁产品是乌克兰经济的基础。在2022年俄罗斯全面入侵开始之前，冶金和采矿业约占乌克兰国民收入的10%和其出口的三分之一。欧盟是其最大客户。但该行业因俄罗斯持续轰炸而遭受损失。自2022年冲突开始以来，乌克兰所有钢铁厂都曾被轰炸，但雷任科夫说，袭击最近“显著加剧”。9月某个时候，乌克兰“没有生产一吨钢铁”，这是大约150年来的第一次，他补充道。自战争开始以来，已有近800名Metinvest工人丧生。雷任科夫说，该公司已“改善了其钢铁厂的掩体区域”，工人们可以在空袭期间在那里避难。“不幸的是，你无法覆盖整个钢铁厂来避免它受损。”雷任科夫说他预计即将到来的冬天将是“我们历史上最艰难的冬天之一”

https://www.myjoyonline.com/over-half-of.title: Over half of South Africa evacuation expenditure lacks invoices – NPP
https://www.myjoyonline.com/over-half-of.summary: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says more than half of the money spent on evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa is not supported by invoices in documents released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/over-half-of.summary_zh: 新爱国党 (NPP) 表示，在外交部公布的文件中，用于从南非撤离加纳人的资金中超过一半没有发票支持。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/over-half-of.body: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says more than half of the money spent on evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa is not supported by invoices in documents released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Speaking at a press briefing on Sunday, October 18, the Communications Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, said GH¢27.18 million was spent on chartered flights, representing about 55 per cent of the total evacuation expenditure, without invoices or contracts provided in the documents cited by the party. He said the Ministry's response to a Right to Information (RTI) request dated September 18, 2026, and its report to Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee did not contain invoices, contracts or the names of the flight operators. "More than half the money comes with no invoice. GHS 27,183,700 was spent on chartered flights. That is 55 per cent of the entire cost. Not one invoice. Not one contract. Not even the name of the operator. Only a sentence saying the flights were arranged. Emergency explains the urgency. It does not excuse the missing receipts," he said. Mr Aboagye questioned why the Ministry had not provided the supporting documents for the charter flights. He also questioned the reported cost of $750,000 for each of three chartered flights, alleging that the amount was significantly higher than the $180,000 to $300,000 he said industry checks suggested was the expected cost of chartering a flight through Ethiopian Airlines or Air Tanzania. The NPP further called for the publication of the original Ethiopian Airlines invoices to establish the actual cost of the flights and address its concerns about possible overbilling. "Information reaching the New Patriotic Party indicates that the first three charter flights were operated by Ethiopian Airlines and arranged through a Mr Vanderpuye. We are further informed that each of those three flights may have been billed at close to USD 300,000 above its true cost. According to the Minister’s own documents, each charter flights cost $750,000. We had 3 chartered flights to lift about 900 passengers. That means, it costs the state $2,500 to buy a seat for a single passenger travelling from South Africa to Ghana. "Our checks from the industry place the maximum cost of chartering a flight from Ethiopian Airlines and Air Tanzania should cost between $180,000 and $300,000 for one. Strangely, the Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs is telling us he paid $750,000 for one airplane. Just one. "We put this to the Minister directly, and we invite him to prove it wrong with paper, not words. Publish the original Ethiopian Airlines invoices for all three flights, so we can have some proper conversation with the airline as to how and why it ripped off the country at such a crucial time. Tell Ghanaians why his Ministry has fallen out with the very man who arranged them."
https://www.myjoyonline.com/over-half-of.title_zh: 南非撤离支出超过一半缺乏发票——NPP
https://www.myjoyonline.com/over-half-of.body_zh: 新爱国党（NPP）表示，在外交部公布的文件中，用于从南非撤离加纳人的资金中超过一半没有发票支持。周日（10月18日）在新闻发布会上，新爱国党（NPP）通讯主任丹尼斯·米拉克斯·阿博阿吉表示，GH¢27.18 million用于包机，约占撤离总支出的55%，而该党引用的文件中没有提供发票或合同。他说，外交部对2026年9月18日提出的信息自由（RTI）请求的答复及其向议会外交事务委员会的报告中没有包含发票、合同或航班运营商的名称。“超过一半的资金没有发票。GHS 27,183,700用于包机。这占总成本的55%。没有一张发票。没有一份合同。甚至没有运营商的名称。只有一句话说航班已安排。紧急情况解释了紧迫性。但它不能成为缺少收据的借口，”他说。阿博阿吉先生质疑为什么外交部没有提供包机支持文件。他还质疑据报每架三架包机中的每一架成本为$750,000，声称这一金额远高于他所说行业调查显示通过埃塞俄比亚航空或坦桑尼亚航空包机的预期成本$180,000至$300,000。新爱国党进一步呼吁公布埃塞俄比亚航空的原始发票，以确定航班的实际成本并解决其对可能超额收费的担忧。“新爱国党收到的信息表明，前三架包机由埃塞俄比亚航空运营，并通过一位Vanderpuye先生安排。我们进一步获悉，这三架航班中的每一架可能被收取了接近其真实成本以上USD 300,000的费用。根据部长自己的文件，每架包机成本$750,000。我们有3架包机来运送约900名乘客。这意味着，国家为从南非到加纳的每位单乘客座位支付$2,500。“我们从行业进行的调查显示，从埃塞俄比亚航空和坦桑尼亚航空包机的最高成本应为每个航班$180,000至$300,000。奇怪的是，尊敬的外交部长告诉我们他为一架飞机支付了$750,000。就一架。“我们直接向部长提出了这一点，并邀请他用文件而不是话语来证明它是错误的。公布所有三架航班的埃塞俄比亚航空原始发票，以便我们能够与航空公司进行一些适当的对话，了解它如何以及为什么在如此关键时刻敲诈这个国家。告诉加纳人为什么他的部与安排这些航班的那个人闹翻了。”

https://saharareporters.com/2026/10/18/n.summary: Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Finance has disputed a figure showing that the Federal Government’s interest payments reached 124 per cent of its revenue in the first half of 2026, describing the interpretation of the data as misleading. The ministry, in a press release issued in Abuja on Sunday, said the figure, attributed to the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update, did not adequately account for the structure of government debt obligations and the timing of revenue collection.
https://saharareporters.com/2026/10/18/n.summary_zh: 尼日利亚联邦财政部对一项显示联邦政府2026年上半年利息支付达到其收入124%的数字提出异议，称对该数据的解读具有误导性。该部周日在阿布贾发布的一份新闻稿中表示，这一归因于世界银行2026年10月《尼日利亚发展更新》的数字没有充分考虑政府债务义务的结构和收入征收的时间。
https://saharareporters.com/2026/10/18/n.body: According to the ministry, the calculation combines debt serviced by the Federal Government on behalf of other tiers of government, including external loans to states, with federal revenue alone, thereby overstating the ratio. Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Finance has disputed a figure showing that the Federal Government’s interest payments reached 124 per cent of its revenue in the first half of 2026, describing the interpretation of the data as misleading. The ministry, in a press release issued in Abuja on Sunday, said the figure, attributed to the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update, did not adequately account for the structure of government debt obligations and the timing of revenue collection. According to the ministry, the calculation combines debt serviced by the Federal Government on behalf of other tiers of government, including external loans to states, with federal revenue alone, thereby overstating the ratio. “The interest figure includes debt the Federal Government services on behalf of other tiers of government, including external loans to states,” the ministry said. The ministry also argued that the revenue figure used in the calculation was incomplete because it excluded independent revenue earned by government agencies and enterprises but not yet remitted to the Treasury. It said revenue collection typically increases in the second half of the year because of the statutory timing of certain tax payments, making a half-year comparison an inadequate measure of the government’s overall fiscal position. The ministry cited the 2025 figures as an example, stating that the interest-to-revenue ratio stood at 156 per cent in the first half of that year, while the full-year debt-service-to-revenue ratio fell below 60 per cent. It said the ratio had declined from 97 per cent before the current administration’s reforms. “This is a clear sign of the progress delivered by the current administration's reforms,” the ministry said. The ministry further defended the government’s fiscal position by comparing revenue and interest payments between the first halves of 2025 and 2026. According to the statement, federal revenue increased by 72 per cent, from N3.6 trillion in the first half of 2025 to N6.2 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026. Interest payments, however, rose by 38 per cent, from N5.6 trillion to N7.7 trillion over the same period. The ministry said the figures showed that revenue was growing almost twice as fast as interest costs. It added that the interest-to-revenue ratio declined by 32 percentage points, from 156 per cent in the first half of 2025 to 124 per cent in the first half of 2026. The gap between interest payments and revenue also narrowed from N2 trillion to N1.5 trillion, according to the ministry. “This is the result of reforms working, not a sign of fiscal distress,” the statement said. The ministry also questioned the use of half-year figures to assess Nigeria’s debt sustainability, arguing that the government’s overall fiscal position should be evaluated using full-year data. “Debt sustainability is assessed on a full-year basis, not over six months,” it said. The ministry cited the World Bank’s reported projection that Nigeria’s full-year debt service in 2026, covering both interest and principal repayments, would amount to 46 per cent of revenue. It described the projection as a more appropriate benchmark for assessing the country’s debt position. The statement comes amid continuing public scrutiny of Nigeria’s debt burden, government revenue and the proportion of public funds devoted to servicing debt. The ministry maintained that the 124 per cent figure, when considered without the broader fiscal context, could create a misleading impression of the country’s financial position. It also defended the legality of the Federal Government’s borrowing, insisting that all loans were obtained within approved limits and in accordance with relevant laws.
https://saharareporters.com/2026/10/18/n.title_zh: 尼日利亚财政部对世界银行124%债务利息与收入数字提出异议
https://saharareporters.com/2026/10/18/n.body_zh: 根据该部说法，这一计算将联邦政府代表其他层级政府偿还的债务（包括向各州的外部贷款）与仅联邦收入相结合，从而夸大了该比率。尼日利亚联邦财政部对一项显示联邦政府2026年上半年利息支付达到其收入124%的数字提出异议，称对该数据的解读具有误导性。该部在周日于阿布贾发布的一份新闻稿中表示，这一归因于世界银行2026年10月《尼日利亚发展更新》的数字，没有充分考虑政府债务义务的结构以及收入征收的时间。根据该部说法，这一计算将联邦政府代表其他层级政府偿还的债务（包括向各州的外部贷款）与仅联邦收入相结合，从而夸大了该比率。“利息数字包括联邦政府代表其他层级政府偿还的债务，包括向各州的外部贷款，”该部表示。该部还辩称，用于计算的收入数字是不完整的，因为它排除了政府机构和企业赚取但尚未汇入国库的独立收入。它表示，由于某些税款的法定缴纳时间，收入征收通常在下半年增加，因此半年比较不足以衡量政府的整体财政状况。该部以2025年数据为例，指出当年上半年的利息与收入比率达到156%，而全年债务服务与收入比率则降至60%以下。它表示，该比率已从当前政府改革前的97%下降。“这是当前政府改革所带来进展的明确迹象，”该部表示。该部还通过比较2025年和2026年上半年的收入和利息支付来为政府的财政状况辩护。根据声明，联邦收入增长72%，从2025年上半年的3.6万亿奈拉增至2026年同期6.2万亿奈拉。然而，利息支付同期增长38%，从5.6万亿奈拉增至7.7万亿奈拉。该部表示，这些数字显示收入增长速度几乎是利息成本的两倍。它补充说，利息与收入比率下降了32个百分点，从2025年上半年的156%降至2026年上半年的124%。根据该部说法，利息支付与收入之间的差距也从2万亿奈拉缩小至1.5万亿奈拉。“这是改革奏效的结果，而不是财政困境的迹象，”声明表示。该部还质疑使用半年数据来评估尼日利亚债务可持续性的做法，认为应使用全年数据来评估政府的整体财政状况。“债务可持续性是按全年基础评估的，而不是六个月，”它表示。该部引用了世界银行报告的预测，即尼日利亚2026年全年债务服务（包括利息和本金偿还）将达到收入的46%。它称这一预测是评估该国债务状况的更合适基准。该声明发布之际，公众继续对尼日利亚的债务负担、政府收入以及用于偿债的公共资金比例进行审查。该部坚持认为，如果不考虑更广泛的财政背景，124%的数字可能会给人造成对该国财务状况的误导印象。它还为联邦政府借款的合法性辩护，坚称所有贷款均在批准的限额内并根据相关法律获得。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.summary: “NLNG has never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single payout.” Mr Onanuga urged the public to disregard the claim. He argued that for the states’ combined share to reach N9 trillion, the total NLNG dividends paid into the Federation Account would have to exceed N33.68 trillion ($25 billion), in a single declaration. “NLNG has never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single payout,” the presidency’s statement read.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.summary_zh: “NLNG 从未一次性向联邦账户支付 250 亿美元的股息。”Onanuga 先生敦促公众忽视这一说法。他认为，要使各州的总份额达到 9 万亿奈拉，注入联邦账户的 NLNG 股息总额必须超过 33.68 万亿奈拉（250 亿美元），一次性申报。“NLNG 从未一次性向联邦账户支付 250 亿美元的股息，”总统府的声明写道。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: Bayo Onanuga, special adviser to President Bola Tinubu on information and strategy, said in a statement on Sunday that the amount claimed by the governor was inconsistent with the revenue-sharing formula and the history of NLNG’s dividend payments to the Federation. Mr Onanuga argued that a one-off payment of N250 billion to each of Nigeria’s 36 states would amount to N9 trillion, excluding the federal government, the Federal Capital Territory and the 774 local government areas. “Under the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) formula, states receive 26.72 per cent of the distributable Federation Account revenue. For the states’ share alone to reach N9 trillion, total NLNG dividends paid into the Federation Account would have to exceed N33.68 trillion (about $25 billion) in a single declaration,” the statement read. “NLNG has never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single payout.” Mr Onanuga urged the public to disregard the claim. “Makinde’s latest claim that the Federal Government is withholding the NLNG dividend windfall is false and should be disregarded.” However, the presidency’s statement did not provide a transaction-by-transaction reconciliation of the specific NLNG dividend proceeds referenced by Mr Makinde or a breakdown of the sums allegedly due to individual states. The dispute followed remarks by Mr Makinde at the 2027 Budget Stakeholders’ Consultative Engagement in Ibadan on Friday, where he alleged that the Federal Government had spent the dividend proceeds instead of distributing the states’ shares. “They fooled us. The Nigeria LNG paid dividends to the Federal Government, which went straight into the Federation Account, but they spent it,” Mr Makinde said, He stated that the amounts due to the states had been reconciled and that each state was expected to receive more than N250 billion. Mr Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement for the upcoming 2027 elections, further alleged that the release of the funds had been postponed until after the 2027 general elections, questioning why political considerations should take precedence over the needs of citizens. “Each state was supposed to get N250 billion. We had already identified projects that would expand Oyo State’s economy. But they have now said the money will not be paid until after the election. Is the election more important than the people of Nigeria?” the governor said. Responding, Mr Onanuga said states receive 26.72 per cent of distributable Federation Account revenue under the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) sharing formula. He argued that for the states’ combined share to reach N9 trillion, the total NLNG dividends paid into the Federation Account would have to exceed N33.68 trillion ($25 billion), in a single declaration. “NLNG has never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single payout,” the presidency’s statement read. According to the statement, NLNG has paid approximately $21.5 billion in dividends to the Federation over the past 25 years, with less than $3 billion realised since Mr Tinubu assumed office. Mr Onanuga argued that the amount allegedly being withheld would therefore exceed the company’s entire historical dividend payments to the Federation. “Therefore, any claim that a single payout exceeds the company’s entire lifetime distribution to the Federation—and is being withheld—defies basic logic and economic reality,” he said

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh: Bayo Onanuga，总统博拉·蒂努布的信息和战略特别顾问，周日在声明中表示，州长声称的金额与收入分享公式以及NLNG向联邦支付股息的历史不符。Onanuga先生辩称，向尼日利亚36个州中的每一个一次性支付2500亿奈拉，总额将达到9万亿奈拉，这还不包括联邦政府、联邦首都区和774个地方政府。声明写道：“根据联邦账户分配委员会（FAAC）公式，各州获得可分配联邦账户收入的26.72%。仅各州的份额就要达到9万亿奈拉，那么一次性宣布支付给联邦账户的NLNG股息总额就必须超过33.68万亿奈拉（约250亿美元）。”“NLNG从未在单次支付中向联邦账户支付250亿美元的股息。”Onanuga先生敦促公众忽视这一说法。“Makinde最近声称联邦政府扣留NLNG股息意外之财，这是虚假的，应该被忽视。”然而，总统府的声明并未提供对Makinde先生提到的具体NLNG股息收益的逐笔交易对账，也没有提供据称应支付给各州的金额明细。这场争端源于Makinde先生周五在伊巴丹举行的2027年预算利益相关者咨询会议上的言论，他指控联邦政府已经花费了股息收益，而不是分配各州的份额。Makinde先生说：“他们愚弄了我们。尼日利亚液化天然气公司向联邦政府支付了股息，这些股息直接进入联邦账户，但他们花掉了它。”他表示，应支付给各州的金额已经核对清楚，每个州预计将收到超过2500亿奈拉。作为2027年即将举行的选举中联合人民运动的总统候选人，Makinde先生进一步指控资金的释放已被推迟到2027年大选之后，并质疑为什么政治考虑应优先于公民的需求。州长说：“每个州本应获得2500亿奈拉。我们已经确定了将扩大奥约州经济的项目。但他们现在说这笔钱要到选举后才会支付。选举比尼日利亚人民更重要吗？”作为回应，Onanuga先生表示，根据联邦账户分配委员会（FAAC）分享公式，各州获得可分配联邦账户收入的26.72%。他辩称，要使各州的合计份额达到9万亿奈拉，支付给联邦账户的NLNG股息总额就必须超过33.68万亿奈拉（250亿美元），这是在单次宣布中的金额。总统府的声明写道：“NLNG从未在单次支付中向联邦账户支付250亿美元的股息。”根据声明，NLNG在过去25年中已向联邦支付约215亿美元的股息，自Tinubu先生上任以来实现的不到30亿美元。Onanuga先生辩称，因此，据称被扣留的金额将超过该公司向联邦支付的整个历史股息总额。他说：“因此，任何声称单次支付超过公司向联邦的整个生命周期分配总额——而且正在被扣留——的说法都违背了基本逻辑和经济现实。”

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.summary: The Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF), an environmental advocacy organisation, has called on the federal government to protect indigenous seeds and farmers’ rights, warning that industrial agricultural practices and restrictive seed policies could undermine food sovereignty, biodiversity, and nutrition.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.summary_zh: 地球母亲健康基金会 (HOMEF) 是一个环境倡导组织，它呼吁联邦政府保护本土种子和农民权利，警告工业化农业实践和限制性种子政策可能破坏粮食主权、生物多样性和营养。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: The Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF), an environmental advocacy organisation, has called on the federal government to protect indigenous seeds and farmers’ rights, warning that industrial agricultural practices and restrictive seed policies could undermine food sovereignty, biodiversity, and nutrition. The organisation made the call on Friday to mark World Food Day, observed annually on 16 October, arguing that hunger and malnutrition persist in resource-rich countries because of political and economic choices that disadvantage smallholder farmers and local food systems. In a statement made available to PREMIUM TIMES by its Media and Communications Manager, Kome Odhomor, HOMEF said food security requires more than increasing agricultural output. It called for policies that protect local seed varieties, promote ecological farming and give farming communities greater control over what they grow and how they produce food. The organisation also called on Nigerians to pay closer attention to the origins and nutritional quality of their food, warning that climate change, economic instability, and conflict continue to threaten food production and distribution. Nnimmo Bassey , HOMEF’s executive director, said Nigeria’s food system was overly dependent on monoculture and cash-crop production, which he noted weakened food supply chains, depleted soil health and reduced farmers’ control over agricultural production. “World Food Day should be a day of reflection. It must also be a day of structural reckoning,” Mr Bassey said, calling for a shift from industrial uniformity towards diverse and ecologically sustainable farming systems. He said indigenous seeds are critical to adapting to climate change because they preserve genetic diversity that can support drought resistance, pest management, and improved nutrition. “We must move beyond the short-sighted goal of ‘yield at any cost’ and support a transition to agroecology,” he said. Agroecology applies ecological principles to agricultural production, emphasising soil health, biodiversity, local knowledge, and sustainable relationships between farming communities and their environment. Mr Bassey said protecting indigenous seeds was essential to preventing biodiversity loss and sustaining ecosystems, arguing that food systems should not sacrifice environmental health for short-term production gains. HOMEF’s Director of Programmes, Joyce Brown, said hunger in resource-rich African countries reflected failures in political and economic decision-making. She said that food should not be treated merely as a commodity for profit but as a fundamental human right connected to public health, cultural identity and community livelihoods. Ms Brown called on governments and international institutions to review policies that, she said, privilege industrial exporters over small-scale farmers who supply local communities. She specifically raised concerns about Nigeria’s Plant Variety Protection Act, 2021, explaining that restrictions on farmers’ ability to save and reuse seeds could threaten the food and nutritional security of vulnerable communities. The law provides a framework for protecting the rights of breeders of new plant varieties. The debate over its implementation includes questions about how breeders’ rights should be balanced with farmers’ traditional practices and access to seeds. Ms Brown said agricultural policies should recognise farmers’ rights and ensure that communities closest to the land retain meaningful authority over what they grow and how they use their resources. Mariann Bassey-Olsson, deputy director of Environmental Rights Action/Friends of the Earth Nigeria , described seed-saving and exchange as essential to farmers’ independence and the preservation of cultural heritage.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.title_zh: 在世界粮食日 HOMEF 敦促联邦政府保护本土种子和农民权利
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh: 地球母亲健康基金会（HOMEF）是一家环境倡导组织，该组织呼吁联邦政府保护本土种子和农民权利，并警告称工业化农业实践和限制性种子政策可能破坏粮食主权、生物多样性和营养。该组织在周五发出这一呼吁，以纪念每年10月16日举行的世界粮食日，认为资源丰富的国家中饥饿和营养不良持续存在，是因为政治和经济选择不利于小农和当地粮食系统。在其媒体和传播经理Kome Odhomor提供给PREMIUM TIMES的一份声明中，HOMEF表示，粮食安全需要的不仅仅是增加农业产量。它呼吁制定保护当地种子品种、促进生态农业并赋予农业社区对其种植内容和粮食生产方式更大控制权的政策。该组织还呼吁尼日利亚人更加关注其食物的来源和营养质量，并警告称气候变化、经济不稳定和冲突继续威胁粮食生产和分配。HOMEF执行主任Nnimmo Bassey表示，尼日利亚的粮食系统过度依赖单一栽培和经济作物生产，他指出这削弱了粮食供应链、耗尽了土壤健康并减少了农民对农业生产的控制。“世界粮食日应该是一个反思的日子。它也必须是一个结构清算的日子，”Bassey先生说，他呼吁从工业化的统一性转向多样化和生态可持续的农业系统。他说，本土种子对于适应气候变化至关重要，因为它们保存了可以支持抗旱、害虫管理和改善营养的遗传多样性。“我们必须超越‘不惜代价提高产量’的短视目标，并支持向农业生态学的转变，”他说。农业生态学将生态原则应用于农业生产，强调土壤健康、生物多样性、当地知识以及农业社区与其环境之间的可持续关系。Bassey先生说，保护本土种子对于防止生物多样性丧失和维持生态系统至关重要，他认为粮食系统不应为了短期生产收益而牺牲环境健康。HOMEF项目主任Joyce Brown表示，资源丰富的非洲国家的饥饿反映了政治和经济决策的失败。她说，粮食不应仅仅被视为利润的商品，而应被视为与公共健康、文化身份和社区生计相关的一项基本人权。Brown女士呼吁各国政府和国际机构审查那些她所说的优先考虑工业出口商而非为当地社区提供粮食的小农的政策。她特别对尼日利亚2021年《植物品种保护法》提出担忧，解释说限制农民保存和重复使用种子的能力可能威胁到脆弱社区的粮食和营养安全。该法律为保护新植物品种育种者的权利提供了框架。对其实施的辩论包括如何平衡育种者权利与农民传统做法和种子获取权的问题。Brown女士说，农业政策应承认农民权利，并确保最接近土地的社区对其种植内容和资源使用方式保留有意义的权威。环境权利行动/尼日利亚地球之友副主任Mariann Bassey-Olsson将保存和交换种子描述为农民独立和保护文化遗产的必要条件。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/promoted/.body: The Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), in partnership with Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited (HEOSL) and Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited, has launched a Human Capacity Development programme to train 48 Nigerians in subsea engineering. The kick-off ceremony took place on Friday, 16 October, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, as part of the Board’s efforts to address critical skills gaps and strengthen indigenous technical expertise in the oil and gas industry. The programme combines six months of classroom instruction with six months of structured on-the-job training, giving participants specialised knowledge and practical experience in subsea engineering. The curriculum covers risers and hydrodynamics engineering, offshore structures design and engineering, pipeline engineering, and computer-aided design and drafting (AutoCAD). “Today marks the beginning of a transformational journey for 48 young Nigerians in a highly specialised field that demands precision, discipline and accountability. Through intensive classroom instruction and structured on-the-job training, the participants will gain hands-on experience in subsea engineering,” he said. Ogbe stressed that subsea operations require technical competence, professionalism and an unwavering commitment to safety. “The competencies you acquire through this programme are critical to the safe, efficient, reliable and environmentally responsible operation of modern oil and gas facilities. Beyond technical proficiency, the training is designed to develop your problem-solving skills, teamwork, professionalism and commitment to safety,” he stated. The Executive Secretary urged the trainees to make the most of the opportunity and demonstrate the discipline and commitment required to succeed in the industry. He expressed confidence that they would emerge with the skills and professional standards needed to contribute to the sector. In his remarks, the Manager, Nigerian Content Development at Heritage Energy, Felix Osiwo, reaffirmed the company’s commitment to indigenous skills development. He noted that a skilled Nigerian workforce is essential to delivering current and future energy infrastructure projects and sustaining industry growth. Earlier in his welcome address, the Managing Director of Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited, George Ebuh, represented by Ifedolapo Aderibigbe, described the programme as a strategic investment by Heritage Energy, NCDMB and Global Oceon in developing indigenous subsea engineering expertise. He noted that skilled local professionals are vital to the safe and reliable operation of offshore and deepwater infrastructure. The trainees expressed appreciation for the opportunity to acquire specialised subsea engineering skills, identifying safety training and AutoCAD as important areas of learning. The programme is part of NCDMB’s Top 10 Field Readiness Human Capacity Development initiatives, designed to address critical skills gaps in the oil and gas industry. It supports the Board’s efforts to develop specialised Nigerian expertise for offshore and deepwater operations, facilitate technology transfer and increase local participation in high-value industry activities. The ceremony was attended by representatives of NCDMB, Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited and Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited, as well as the trainees, facilitators and other industry stakeholders
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/promoted/.title_zh: NCDMB 和 Heritage Energy 为48名尼日利亚人提供海底工程培训
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/promoted/.body_zh: 尼日利亚本地内容开发与监督委员会（NCDMB）与Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited（HEOSL）和Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited合作，启动了一项人力能力开发计划，将培训48名尼日利亚人从事海底工程。该启动仪式于10月16日星期五在河流州哈科特港举行，这是该委员会为解决石油和天然气行业关键技能差距并加强本土技术专长所做努力的一部分。该计划将六个月的课堂教学与六个月的结构化在职培训相结合，为参与者提供海底工程的专业知识和实践经验。课程涵盖立管与流体力学工程、离岸结构设计与工程、管道工程以及计算机辅助设计和绘图（AutoCAD）。“今天标志着48名年轻尼日利亚人在一个高度专业化领域转型之旅的开始，该领域要求精确、纪律和问责。通过密集的课堂教学和结构化在职培训，参与者将获得海底工程的实践经验，”他说。Ogbe强调，海底作业需要技术能力、专业精神和对安全的坚定承诺。“你们通过该计划获得的技能对于现代石油和天然气设施的安全、高效、可靠和环境负责任的运营至关重要。除了技术熟练度之外，该培训旨在培养你们的解决问题能力、团队合作、专业精神和对安全的承诺，”他表示。执行秘书敦促受训者充分利用这一机会，并展示在行业中取得成功所需的纪律和承诺。他表示相信，他们将掌握所需的技能和专业标准，为该部门做出贡献。在他的讲话中，Heritage Energy尼日利亚本地内容开发经理Felix Osiwo重申了公司对本土技能开发的承诺。他指出，一支熟练的尼日利亚劳动力对于交付当前和未来的能源基础设施项目以及维持行业增长至关重要。早些时候，在他的欢迎致辞中，Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited总经理George Ebuh（由Ifedolapo Aderibigbe代表）将该计划描述为Heritage Energy、NCDMB和Global Oceon在开发本土海底工程专长方面的战略投资。他指出，熟练的本地专业人员对于海上和深水基础设施的安全和可靠运营至关重要。受训者对获得专业海底工程技能的机会表示感谢，并将安全培训和AutoCAD确定为重要的学习领域。该计划是NCDMB十大现场准备人力能力开发举措的一部分，旨在解决石油和天然气行业的关键技能差距。它支持该委员会为海上和深水作业开发专业的尼日利亚专长、促进技术转移以及增加本地参与高价值行业活动的努力。出席仪式的有NCDMB、Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited和Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited的代表，以及受训者、培训师和其他行业利益相关者。

https://leadership.ng/buhari-saw-tinubu-.title: Buhari Saw Tinubu As ‘Bad News’ For Nigeria, Resisted His Presidency – Baba-Ahmed
https://leadership.ng/buhari-saw-tinubu-.summary: Baba-Ahmed made the allegation at a summit organised by the Northern Elders Forum, where he accused Tinubu’s administration of taking the country to an unprecedented low and urged Nigerians to reject any attempt to prioritise the president’s second-term ambition over the national interest. “Even Buhari saw Tinubu as bad news for this country.
https://leadership.ng/buhari-saw-tinubu-.summary_zh: Baba-Ahmed 在北方长老论坛组织的一次峰会上提出了这一指控，他指责 Tinubu 政府将国家带到了前所未有的低点，并敦促尼日利亚人拒绝任何将总统第二任期野心置于国家利益之上的企图。“即使是布哈里也认为 Tinubu 对这个国家来说是个坏消息。
https://leadership.ng/buhari-saw-tinubu-.body: Baba-Ahmed made the allegation at a summit organised by the Northern Elders Forum, where he accused Tinubu’s administration of taking the country to an unprecedented low and urged Nigerians to reject any attempt to prioritise the president’s second-term ambition over the national interest. Speaking in a video of the event published on Symfoni’s YouTube channel, the PRP chairman said Nigerians should have questioned Tinubu’s presidential ambition when he adopted the slogan “Emilokan” during the build-up to the 2023 general election. The Yoruba expression, which means “it is my turn”, became one of the defining slogans of Tinubu’s campaign. “Even Buhari saw Tinubu as bad news for this country. In fairness to him, he is not around him. Buhari resisted some people who insisted it had to be Tinubu,” he said. Baba-Ahmed questioned the appropriateness of presenting the presidency as an entitlement, arguing that leading a country with an estimated population of 250 million should not be framed in terms of an individual’s turn to occupy the office. “Nigerians ought to have known there was something wrong the day Tinubu said ‘It’s my turn’. Maybe we missed it,” he said. “We have a presidency of a country of 250 million people. My turn? To do what? To become president”, he added. The PRP chairman also accused the Tinubu administration of worsening the country’s condition since assuming office, insisting that Nigeria could not afford further deterioration. “Now we are being depressed for having a president for three and a half years. He has dragged the country as low as it can go. And it has to stop him. We cannot go below, beyond where we are,” Baba-Ahmed said. He further alleged that the president was more concerned about fulfilling his political ambition than addressing the challenges facing Nigerians. “We will not allow a president to fulfil an ambition that one individual alone can wreak on his country, just to prove that he has the power and the money to do so,” he said. “We are at the bottom. There is no way to go anymore. Every index of failure shows in this administration”, he added. Baba-Ahmed also criticised Tinubu for allegedly failing to make a personal appeal to Nigerians for another term in office, claiming that the president had instead depended on political associates to promote his re-election bid. He equally faulted governors in the North for failing to adequately communicate the region’s economic difficulties and growing dissatisfaction to the president. Despite his criticism of the administration, the PRP chairman expressed optimism that Nigeria would overcome its current challenges, citing the resilience the country had demonstrated during previous crises. “We are very resilient people. We have seen crises bigger than this, and we survived them. We survived it, and we will survive this one. “We will survive the four years of abuse, neglect, and plunder that Tinubu has caused because Nigeria has to survive for our children and their children”, he said. 2027: Opposition Parties Working To Unite Against Tinubu On the 2027 presidential election, Baba-Ahmed said opposition parties were making efforts to form a coalition capable of defeating Tinubu at the polls. He described the proposed alliance as a serious attempt by political actors to set aside their differences and build a common front against the president. “What we have seen is an incredible willingness for politicians to come together and say, let’s put aside some of our differences and see if we can actually create a momentum strong enough to remove this Tinubu,” he said. Baba-Ahmed said the coalition would field a candidate to challenge Tinubu, urging Nigerians who oppose the president’s re-election to support whoever emerges as its flag-bearer. The proposed alliance comes amid growing efforts by opposition figures to consolidate their political strength ahead of the 2027 general election.
https://leadership.ng/buhari-saw-tinubu-.title_zh: 布哈里视蒂努布为尼日利亚的‘坏消息’ 并曾抵制其总统职位——巴巴-艾哈迈德
https://leadership.ng/buhari-saw-tinubu-.body_zh: Baba-Ahmed 在由北方长老论坛组织的峰会上提出了这一指控，他在会上指责 Tinubu 政府将国家带到了前所未有的低谷，并敦促尼日利亚人拒绝任何将总统第二任期野心置于国家利益之上的企图。在 Symfoni 的 YouTube 频道发布的峰会视频中，PRP 主席表示，尼日利亚人本应在 Tinubu 为 2023 年大选造势期间采用“Emilokan”口号时就质疑他的总统野心。这个约鲁巴语表达的意思是“轮到我了”，成为 Tinubu 竞选活动最具标志性的口号之一。“即使是 Buhari 也认为 Tinubu 对这个国家来说是个坏消息。公平地说，他没有和他走得很近。Buhari 抵制了一些坚持必须是 Tinubu 的人，”他说。Baba-Ahmed 质疑将总统职位呈现为一种应得权利的恰当性，认为领导一个估计有 2.5 亿人口的国家不应被框定为某个个人的轮次来担任这一职务。“尼日利亚人本应在 Tinubu 说出‘轮到我了’的那一天就知道出了问题。也许我们错过了，”他说。“我们有一个 2.5 亿人口国家的总统职位。我的轮次？做什么？成为总统”，他补充道。PRP 主席还指责 Tinubu 政府自上台以来恶化了国家的状况，坚持认为尼日利亚无法承受进一步的恶化。“现在我们因为有一个总统三年半而感到沮丧。他把国家拖到了它能到的最低点。而且必须阻止他。我们不能再往下走，不能超出我们现在的位置，”Baba-Ahmed 说。他进一步指称，总统更关心实现自己的政治野心，而不是解决尼日利亚人面临的挑战。“我们不会允许一位总统去实现一个仅仅一个人就能给他的国家带来的野心，只是为了证明他有权力和金钱这样做，”他说。“我们处于底部。再也没有路可走了。这届政府的每一个失败指标都显现出来”，他补充道。Baba-Ahmed 还批评 Tinubu 据称未能亲自向尼日利亚人呼吁连任，声称总统反而依赖政治伙伴来推动他的竞选连任。他同样指责北方的州长未能充分向总统传达该地区的经济困难和日益增长的不满。尽管他对政府提出批评，PRP 主席仍对尼日利亚能够克服当前挑战表示乐观，引用了该国在以往危机中表现出的韧性。“我们是非常有韧性的人民。我们见过比这更大的危机，我们挺过来了。我们挺过来了，我们也会挺过这一次。“我们将挺过 Tinubu 造成的四年滥权、忽视和掠夺，因为尼日利亚必须为了我们的孩子和他们的孩子而生存下去”，他说。2027 年：反对党正努力团结起来反对 Tinubu 关于 2027 年总统选举，Baba-Ahmed 表示反对党正在努力组建一个能够在投票中击败 Tinubu 的联盟。他将拟议的联盟描述为政治行为者认真尝试搁置分歧并建立共同阵线来对抗总统。“我们看到的是政客们令人难以置信的意愿，他们走到一起说，让我们搁置我们的一些分歧，看看我们是否真的能创造足够强大的势头来移除这个 Tinubu，”他说。Baba-Ahmed 表示，该联盟将推出一名候选人来挑战 Tinubu，并敦促反对总统连任的尼日利亚人支持无论谁成为其旗手。这一拟议联盟是在反对派人物在 2027 年大选前努力巩固其政治力量的背景下提出的。

https://leadership.ng/n250b-nlng-fund-pu.title: N250b NLNG Fund: Publish The Dividend Receipts, Makinde-Daura Campaign Replies Presidency
https://leadership.ng/n250b-nlng-fund-pu.summary: “We therefore challenge the Presidency to publish the relevant NLNG dividend receipts, Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) decisions and official communications establishing the amounts received, the sums approved for distribution and the timing of the proposed payments to states,” it said.
https://leadership.ng/n250b-nlng-fund-pu.summary_zh: “因此，我们敦促总统府公布相关的 NLNG 股息收入、联邦账户分配委员会 (FAAC) 决定以及官方通讯，以确定收到的金额、批准分配的款项以及拟向各州支付的时间，”它说。
https://leadership.ng/n250b-nlng-fund-pu.body: The MDPCO said its attention was drawn to what it described as a lame attempt by the Tinubu Presidency to evade the core issues raised by Makinde that NLNG dividends accruable to states are being withheld by the Federal Government. It added, “If the Tinubu Presidency claims that Engr. Makinde is wrong in his assertion that N250 billion NLNG dividend meant for states is being withheld, we challenge President Tinubu to directly tell Nigerians if the said dividends have been paid to the states rather than resorting to personal attacks on the APM presidential candidate. The organisation questioned the constitutional basis for withholding funds meant for states. “Moreover, and importantly, does the Presidency have any constitutional power to withhold any funds accruing to the states in a federation? “We therefore challenge the Presidency to publish the relevant NLNG dividend receipts, Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) decisions and official communications establishing the amounts received, the sums approved for distribution and the timing of the proposed payments to states,” it said. According to the MDPCO, Nigerians deserve clear answers to three fundamental questions: how much NLNG paid in dividends during the period under discussion and the amount credited to the Federation Account, and how much was approved for distribution to the states. “Invoking NLNG’s cumulative dividend payments in the last 25 years does not answer these questions. Historical totals cannot, by themselves, establish the amount received during a specific period and the sum available for distribution. It does not answer whether a particular payment was proposed, approved, received, delayed or withheld. Those questions can only be settled by the relevant financial records. “If the Presidency’s argument is that allocating ₦250 billion to each of the 36 states would amount to ₦9 trillion, a sum NLNG has never paid as a single dividend as it alleged, that calculation does not resolve the matter. The question is not whether ₦9 trillion was ever paid in a single transaction, but the amount that is actually under discussion as can be established by the official records,” the organisation stated. The MDPCO defended Makinde’s integrity, saying he is not given to propaganda. “Engr. Makinde, the Governor of Oyo State and presidential candidate of the APM, is known for his integrity. He is not given to propaganda and disinformation which are the known stock-in-trade and policy direction of the Tinubu-led All Progressives Congress (APC) administration. He has maintained a clean, issue-based campaign devoid of mudslinging, misinformation, disinformation and propaganda for which the APC is known. “The MDPCO stands by Engr. Makinde in his assertion that President Tinubu is running a voodoo economy where government thrives on lies, where the national fortunes only improve on paper with no corresponding improvement in the harsh everyday life of citizens under his administration.” It added that the Presidency is jittery over Makinde’s growing popularity. “In any event, our campaign is aware that President Tinubu and his APC have been jittery and restless over Engr. Makinde’s soaring popularity and the widespread acceptance of his RESET NIGERIA Agenda message across the nation since the commencement of the campaign. “The Tinubu Presidency is disturbed because Nigerians have identified Engr. Makinde as a credible alternative to President Tinubu, leading to the massive surge to his campaign and the APM. It should therefore come to terms with the fact that no amount of propaganda and lies against Engr. Makinde will help President Tinubu at this time,” it said. The attention of the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organization (MDPCO) has been drawn to the lame attempt by the Tinubu Presidency to evade the core issues raised by the Presidential Candidate of the Allied People’s Movement (APM) and Governor of Oyo State, Engr.
https://leadership.ng/n250b-nlng-fund-pu.title_zh: 2500亿奈拉NLNG基金：公布分红收据，马金德-道拉竞选团队回应总统府
https://leadership.ng/n250b-nlng-fund-pu.body_zh: MDPCO表示，其注意力被吸引到它所描述的蒂努布总统为回避马金德提出的核心问题而进行的蹩脚尝试，即应支付给各州的NLNG股息正被联邦政府扣留。它补充说：“如果蒂努布总统声称恩格·马金德关于2500亿奈拉NLNG股息本应支付给各州却被扣留的说法是错误的，我们挑战蒂努布总统直接告诉尼日利亚人，上述股息是否已支付给各州，而不是诉诸对APM总统候选人的个人攻击。该组织质疑扣留本应支付给各州的资金的宪法依据。“此外，重要的是，总统府是否有任何宪法权力扣留联邦制下应支付给各州的任何资金？“因此，我们挑战总统府公布相关的NLNG股息收据、联邦账户分配委员会（FAAC）决定以及官方通讯，以确立已收到的金额、批准分配的金额以及拟向各州支付的时间，”它说。根据MDPCO的说法，尼日利亚人值得就三个基本问题得到明确答案：在讨论期间NLNG支付了多少股息、记入联邦账户的金额是多少，以及批准分配给各州的金额是多少。“援引NLNG过去25年的累计股息支付并不能回答这些问题。历史总额本身无法确立特定时期内收到的金额以及可供分配的金额。它无法回答是否提出了某笔付款、是否获得批准、是否收到、是否延迟或是否被扣留。这些问题只能通过相关财务记录来解决。“如果总统府的论点是，将2500亿奈拉分配给36个州中的每一个将达到9万亿奈拉，这是NLNG从未作为单一股息支付过的金额，正如它所声称的那样，这种计算并不能解决这个问题。问题不在于是否曾以单一交易支付9万亿奈拉，而是实际上正在讨论的金额，这可以通过官方记录来确立，”该组织指出。MDPCO为马金德的诚信辩护，称他不搞宣传。“恩格·马金德，奥约州州长和APM总统候选人，以其诚信闻名。他不搞宣传和虚假信息，而这些正是蒂努布领导的全进步大会党（APC）政府的已知惯用伎俩和政策方向。他一直保持着基于问题的干净竞选，没有诽谤、错误信息、虚假信息和宣传，而这些正是APC所闻名的。“MDPCO支持恩格·马金德的说法，即蒂努布总统正在运行一个巫毒经济，政府靠谎言 thriving，国家财富只在纸面上改善，而在其政府下公民日常严酷生活中没有相应的改善。”它补充说，总统府对马金德日益增长的受欢迎程度感到不安。“无论如何，我们的竞选活动意识到，自竞选开始以来，蒂努布总统及其APC对恩格·马金德飙升的人气以及全国范围内对其RESET NIGERIA议程信息的广泛接受一直感到不安和焦躁。“蒂努布总统府感到不安，因为尼日利亚人已将恩格·马金德视为蒂努布总统的可信替代者，导致对其竞选和APM的大规模涌入。因此，它应该接受这样一个事实，即此时任何针对恩格·马金德的宣传和谎言都无法帮助蒂努布总统，”它说。马金德-道拉总统竞选组织（MDPCO）的注意力被吸引到蒂努布总统为回避APM总统候选人和奥约州州长恩格提出的核心问题而进行的蹩脚尝试。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title: Finance Ministry faults claim that FG’s interest payments hit 124% of revenue
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary: The Federal Ministry of Finance has disputed a claim that the Federal Government’s interest payments reached 124 per cent of its revenue in the first half of 2026, describing the figure as misleading. The ministry said recent analysis and public commentary, which cited the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update, compared mismatched interest figures against an incomplete revenue base.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary_zh: 联邦财政部驳斥了联邦政府2026年上半年利息支付达到其收入124%的说法，称该数字具有误导性。该部表示，最近的分析和公众评论引用了世界银行2026年10月尼日利亚发展更新，将不匹配的利息数字与不完整的收入基础进行了比较。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body: The Federal Ministry of Finance has disputed a claim that the Federal Government’s interest payments reached 124 per cent of its revenue in the first half of 2026, describing the figure as misleading. The ministry said recent analysis and public commentary, which cited the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update, compared mismatched interest figures against an incomplete revenue base. In a statement released on Sunday, the ministry said the 124 per cent interest calculation includes the debt serviced by the federal government on behalf of other tiers of government, including external loans to states. “Measuring this against federal revenue alone overstates the ratio, which is only meaningful when debt and revenue cover the same level of government,” the statement said. The ministry also asserted that the reported revenue is incomplete as it excludes the independent revenue earned by government agencies and enterprises but not yet remitted to the treasury. “In addition, more revenue is typically earned in the second half of the year than in the first due to the statutory timing of certain payments. This is why the ratio stood at 156% in H1 2025, while the full-year 2025 debt service-to-revenue ratio was below 60%, down from 97% before the reforms,” it stated. The ministry explained that federal revenue rose by 72 per cent from ₦3.6 trillion in the first half of 2025 to ₦6.2 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026. Interest payments, however, rose by 38 per cent, from ₦5.6 trillion to ₦7.7 trillion over the same period, according to the ministry. “The interest-to-revenue ratio fell by 32 percentage points in a single year, from 156% to 124%, and the gap between interest and revenue narrowed from ₦2.0 trillion to ₦1.5 trillion,” the ministry said. The ministry attributed the changes to the current administration’s economic reforms, arguing that revenue is growing faster than interest costs. It argued that a six-month figure alone should not be used to evaluate the sustainability of government debt. “Debt sustainability is assessed on a full-year basis, not over six months,” the statement said. Citing the World Bank report, the ministry said Nigeria’s full-year 2026 debt service, covering both interest and principal, is projected at 46 per cent of revenue, and that this forecast is the appropriate benchmark for assessing the country’s debt-service burden. The ministry noted that all borrowing falls within the limits approved by the National Assembly under the 2026 Appropriation Act and the approved borrowing plan, in compliance with the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2007 and the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act 2003. “We encourage analysts and commentators to apply the same rigour they seek to hold the government to: compare like with like, read figures in context, and seek clarification where the data is unclear,” the ministry said
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title_zh: 财政部对联邦政府利息支付达到收入124%的说法提出异议
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body_zh: 联邦财政部驳斥了联邦政府2026年上半年利息支付达到其收入124%的说法，称该数字具有误导性。该部表示，最近的分析和公开评论引用了世界银行2026年10月《尼日利亚发展更新》，将不匹配的利息数字与不完整的收入基数进行了比较。在周日发布的一份声明中，该部表示，124%的利息计算包括联邦政府代表其他层级政府偿还的债务，包括向各州的外部贷款。“仅将其与联邦收入进行对比会夸大这一比率，只有当债务和收入涵盖同一层级政府时，该比率才有意义，”声明称。该部还断言，所报告的收入是不完整的，因为它排除了政府机构和企业赚取但尚未汇入国库的独立收入。“此外，由于某些支付的法定时间安排，下半年通常比上半年赚取更多收入。这就是为什么2025年上半年该比率达到156%，而2025年全年债务偿付与收入比率低于60%，较改革前的97%有所下降，”它指出。该部解释称，联邦收入较2025年上半年的3.6万亿奈拉增长72%，达到2026年同期6.2万亿奈拉。然而，根据该部数据，利息支付同期增长38%，从5.6万亿奈拉增至7.7万亿奈拉。“利息与收入比率在一年内下降了32个百分点，从156%降至124%，利息与收入之间的差距从2.0万亿奈拉缩小至1.5万亿奈拉，”该部表示。该部将这些变化归因于现任政府的经济改革，认为收入增长快于利息成本。它辩称，不应仅使用六个月的数据来评估政府债务的可持续性。“债务可持续性是基于全年进行评估，而不是六个月，”声明称。该部引用世界银行报告称，尼日利亚2026年全年债务偿付（包括利息和本金）预计占收入的46%，这一预测是评估该国债务偿付负担的适当基准。该部指出，所有借款均在2026年拨款法和批准的借款计划下由国民议会批准的限额范围内，符合2007年《财政责任法》和2003年《债务管理办公室（设立）法》。“我们鼓励分析人士和评论员应用他们要求政府遵守的同样严谨态度：比较同类数据，在上下文中阅读数字，并在数据不清晰时寻求澄清，”该部表示

https://businessday.ng/life/article/afri.body: Listen to this article Share Advertisement Nigeria’s government is preparing a new wave of policy reforms targeting creative technology and film distribution as it seeks to position African cinema for expansion into global markets. Speaking at a press briefing in Lagos to announce the activities of 2026 AFRIFF Week, Hannatu Musawa, Minister of Art, Culture and the Creative Economy, officially announced the launch of the 15th edition of the Africa International Film Festival. Musawa, represented by Shaibu Husseini, director-general of the National Film and Video Censors Board (NFVCB), highlighted the festival’s decade-and-a-half milestone as a critical milestone for the continent’s entertainment industry, framing the creative economy as a major engine for economic growth. “For fifteen years, AFRIFF has not merely been a date on our calendar — it has been a monument to African storytelling, a catalyst for economic growth within the creative sector, and a beacon that has been pushing local genius to the global stage,” Husseini said. Central to this year’s festival theme, “Frames of the Future,” is a government commitment to modernize regulatory and support frameworks for local filmmakers. The ministry confirmed it is actively reshaping federal policies to improve distribution infrastructure, spur tech adoption, and foster international co-productions. This key bottleneck has historically constrained monetization across the African film market. She urged African creators to embrace cutting-edge production technology, novel storytelling methods, and cross-border partnerships to compete globally. While laying out a forward-looking vision, she paid tribute to AFRIFF’s leadership and founding visionaries for sustaining institutional excellence and capacity building over 15 years. Ude noted that while early deliberations focused on the disruptive role of artificial intelligence and emerging tech, initial programming data revealed a striking demographic shift: women directed and produced 85 percent of the feature films selected for this year’s screening lineup. To bridge industry talk with operational execution, this year’s festival program will heavily emphasize targeted panels designed to resolve persistent financing bottlenecks, bringing together key dealmakers to establish clear pathways for project funding and execution across the continent. The festival is also seeing a sharp surge in international interest, particularly from North American industry players, following last year’s record engagements; project financing discussions range from $5 million to over $20 million—a trend organisers attribute to aggressive global outreach and expanding market confidence. Underscoring the growing role of private capital in scaling Nigeria’s creative economy, Joelle Haykal, group executive director of Mikano International Limited, said that corporate involvement must extend beyond traditional commercial sponsorship toward long-term local investment and brand building. Haykal emphasized that operating in Nigeria carries a broader mandate to cultivate domestic talent and export the country’s economic and creative potential to global markets. Advocating for responsible corporate citizenship, Haykal called on consumers and regulators to back enterprises that actively reinvest in national economic development, noting that corporate partnerships with platform drivers like AFRIFF are essential for building a resilient national economy. The festival is scheduled to take place in Lagos from November 1 to 7, 2026
https://businessday.ng/life/article/afri.title_zh: 非洲电影节15周年：尼日利亚承诺政策改革以推动非洲电影
https://businessday.ng/life/article/afri.body_zh: 尼日利亚政府正在准备新一轮针对创意科技和电影发行领域的政策改革，以期将非洲电影定位为向全球市场扩张的力量。在拉各斯举行的新闻发布会上，艺术、文化和创意经济部长汉娜图·穆萨瓦宣布2026年AFRIFF周的活动，她正式宣布第15届非洲国际电影节启动。穆萨瓦由国家电影和录像审查委员会（NFVCB）总干事沙伊布·侯赛尼代表，她强调该电影节十五周年的里程碑是非洲娱乐业的关键里程碑，并将创意经济定位为经济增长的主要引擎。“十五年来，AFRIFF不仅仅是我们日历上的一个日期——它一直是非洲叙事的丰碑，是创意领域经济增长的催化剂，也是一座推动本地天才走向全球舞台的灯塔，”侯赛尼说。今年电影节的主题“未来的框架”的核心是政府致力于为本地电影制作人现代化监管和支持框架。该部确认正在积极重塑联邦政策，以改善发行基础设施、刺激技术采用并促进国际联合制作。这一关键瓶颈历史上限制了整个非洲电影市场的货币化。她敦促非洲创作者拥抱前沿制作技术、新颖叙事方法和跨境伙伴关系，以在全球竞争中脱颖而出。在提出前瞻性愿景的同时，她向AFRIFF的领导层和创始愿景者致敬，感谢他们在15年来维持机构卓越和能力建设。乌德指出，虽然早期讨论重点是人工智能和新兴技术的颠覆性作用，但初步编程数据显示出显著的人口结构转变：女性执导和制作了今年入选放映阵容的85%的故事片。为了将行业讨论与实际执行相结合，今年的电影节节目将重点强调旨在解决持续融资瓶颈的针对性小组讨论，汇聚关键交易撮合者，以在整个非洲大陆为项目融资和执行建立明确途径。该电影节还看到国际兴趣急剧上升，特别是来自北美行业参与者的兴趣，这是在去年创纪录参与之后；项目融资讨论范围从500万美元到超过2000万美元——组织者将这一趋势归因于积极的全球外展和不断扩大的市场信心。在强调私人资本在扩大尼日利亚创意经济中的日益重要作用时，Mikano International Limited集团执行董事乔尔·海卡尔表示，企业参与必须超越传统的商业赞助，转向长期本地投资和品牌建设。海卡尔强调，在尼日利亚运营肩负更广泛的使命，即培养国内人才并将该国的经济和创意潜力出口到全球市场。在倡导负责任的企业公民身份时，海卡尔呼吁消费者和监管机构支持那些积极再投资于国家经济发展的企业，并指出企业与AFRIFF等平台驱动者的伙伴关系对于建设有韧性的国民经济至关重要。该电影节定于2026年11月1日至7日在拉各斯举行

https://businessday.ng/news/article/chin.body: Listen to this article Share Advertisement The Chinese Embassy in Nigeria, the Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria (FRCN), have called for expanded content, stronger digital engagement and increased youth participation in the *Ni Hao! China* radio programme to deepen cultural exchanges between Nigeria and China. The call was made on Thursday during a ceremony marking 456 days of the Chinese-language radio programme at the China Cultural Centre in Nigeria, Abuja, where stakeholders highlighted the role of broadcasting in strengthening people-to-people relations beyond conventional diplomatic and economic engagements. Yang Jianxing, Cultural Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria and Director of the China Cultural Centre, said the programme, jointly produced by the embassy and FRCN, had become an important platform for promoting friendship, cultural understanding and mutual learning since its launch in July 2025. Jianxing said the programme had provided Nigerian audiences with an accessible avenue to learn Mandarin and gain insights into China’s history, traditions, food, technological development and everyday life. He said its availability on FRCN radio stations, the corporation’s website, YouTube and other digital platforms had made Chinese-language learning more convenient, but stressed the need to expand its audience and improve its content, particularly to attract younger Nigerians. The diplomat outlined three priorities for the programme’s next phase: enriching its content, adopting innovative approaches to audience engagement and encouraging greater youth participation. He said the programme should sustain its Chinese-language lessons while expanding coverage to tourism, education, culture and other aspects of life in China. He also called for lessons that would enable Nigerians to explain their own cultures, traditions and everyday experiences in Chinese. According to him, the approach would strengthen the programme’s role as a platform for two-way cultural exchange, allowing Nigerians to communicate their cultural identity to Chinese audiences while learning about Chinese society. Jianxing also urged the production team to combine conventional radio broadcasting with short videos, social media, digital learning resources and physical cultural activities to reach audiences whose media consumption increasingly takes place online. He said greater youth participation in language learning, cultural experiences and exchange activities could help develop a new generation of Nigerians capable of promoting friendship and cooperation between the two countries. The diplomat described *Ni Hao! China* as both a reflection of Nigeria-China relations and a contributor to their continued development, noting that the two countries were marking 55 years of diplomatic relations in 2026. He said the relationship had expanded across political engagement, trade, economic cooperation and cultural exchanges, adding that initiatives that brought citizens closer could complement official diplomatic engagements. Jianxing also linked the programme to the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges, describing the initiative as an opportunity to deepen cultural engagement and promote mutual learning between Chinese and African societies. He commended FRCN’s management, production team, language instructors and other Nigerian and Chinese contributors for sustaining the programme. The diplomat expressed appreciation to listeners and media practitioners for their support, saying continued collaboration would help the programme reach more Nigerians and strengthen bilateral cultural relations. Mohammed Babagana, Director-General of FRCN, said the partnership had demonstrated how broadcasting could strengthen relations between countries by promoting cultural awareness and understanding beyond trade, infrastructure and diplomacy.
https://businessday.ng/news/article/chin.title_zh: 中尼广播节目在456天后寻求更广泛覆盖和青年参与
https://businessday.ng/news/article/chin.body_zh: 中国驻尼日利亚大使馆、尼日利亚联邦广播公司（FRCN）呼吁扩大内容、加强数字互动并增加青年参与《你好！中国》广播节目，以深化尼日利亚与中国的文化交流。这一呼吁是在星期四于尼日利亚阿布贾中国文化中心举行的庆祝该中文广播节目开播456天的仪式上提出的，与会利益相关方强调了广播在超越传统外交和经济互动之外加强人民之间关系的作用。中国驻尼日利亚大使馆文化参赞兼中国文化中心主任杨建兴表示，该节目由大使馆和FRCN联合制作，自2025年7月推出以来，已成为促进友谊、文化理解和相互学习的重要平台。建兴表示，该节目为尼日利亚听众提供了一个便捷渠道来学习普通话，并深入了解中国的历史、传统、美食、技术发展和日常生活。他说，该节目在FRCN广播电台、公司网站、YouTube和其他数字平台上的可用性使中文学习更加便利，但强调需要扩大受众并改进内容，特别是吸引年轻的尼日利亚人。这位外交官概述了该节目下一阶段的三个优先事项：丰富其内容、采用创新方法吸引受众并鼓励更大的青年参与。他说，该节目应维持其中文课程，同时扩大对中国旅游、教育、文化和其他生活方面的报道。他还呼吁开设能让尼日利亚人用中文解释自己文化、传统和日常经历的课程。据他介绍，这种方法将加强该节目作为双向文化交流平台的作用，让尼日利亚人能够向中国听众传达他们的文化身份，同时了解中国社会。建兴还敦促制作团队将传统无线电广播与短视频、社交媒体、数字学习资源和实体文化活动相结合，以接触那些媒体消费日益转向线上的受众。他说，增加青年在语言学习、文化体验和交流活动中的参与，可以帮助培养新一代尼日利亚人，他们有能力促进两国之间的友谊与合作。这位外交官将《你好！中国》描述为尼中关系的反映，也是对其持续发展的贡献，并指出两国将在2026年庆祝外交关系55周年。他说，这种关系已在政治互动、贸易、经济合作和文化交流等领域扩展，并补充说，拉近公民距离的举措可以补充官方外交互动。建兴还将该节目与中非人文交流年联系起来，将这一举措描述为深化文化互动并促进中国和非洲社会之间相互学习的机会。他赞扬了FRCN的管理层、制作团队、语言教师和其他尼日利亚和中国贡献者为维持该节目所做的努力。这位外交官对听众和媒体从业者表示感谢，说持续合作将帮助该节目触及更多尼日利亚人并加强双边文化关系。FRCN总干事穆罕默德·巴巴加纳表示，这一伙伴关系展示了广播如何通过促进超越贸易、基础设施和外交的文化意识和理解来加强国家之间的关系。

https://punchng.com/fg-faults-world-bank.summary: The Federal Ministry of Finance described reports that interest payments consumed 124 per cent of the FG’s revenue in the first half of 2026 as misleading, arguing that the calculation relied on incomplete revenue figures and failed to account for debt obligations serviced on behalf of state governments.
https://punchng.com/fg-faults-world-bank.summary_zh: 联邦财政部称，关于利息支付消耗了 2026 年上半年联邦政府收入 124% 的报道具有误导性，认为该计算依赖不完整的收入数据，且未考虑代表州政府偿还的债务义务。
https://punchng.com/fg-faults-world-bank.body: The Federal Ministry of Finance described reports that interest payments consumed 124 per cent of the FG’s revenue in the first half of 2026 as misleading, arguing that the calculation relied on incomplete revenue figures and failed to account for debt obligations serviced on behalf of state governments. The ministry made its position known in a statement on Sunday, which was shared by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, via his X handle. It maintained that every naira borrowed fell within the limits authorised by the National Assembly under the 2026 Appropriation Act and the approved borrowing plan. According to the statement, government borrowing complied with the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2007 and the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act 2003, while details of the country’s debt obligations were regularly published by the DMO. “This is the result of reforms working, not a sign of fiscal distress,” the ministry declared. It also rejected the use of a six-month fiscal snapshot as a definitive measure of debt sustainability, insisting that full-year projections provided a more appropriate assessment. “The same World Bank report projects Nigeria’s full-year 2026 debt service, covering both interest and principal, at 46 per cent of revenue. This is the appropriate benchmark, and a guide to avoid the invalid conclusions being drawn,” the statement read
https://punchng.com/fg-faults-world-bank.title_zh: 联邦政府质疑世界银行数据，驳斥债务担忧
https://punchng.com/fg-faults-world-bank.body_zh: 联邦财政部称，有报道称2026年上半年利息支付消耗了联邦政府收入的124%，这种说法具有误导性。该部辩称，这一计算依赖于不完整的收入数据，且未考虑代表州政府偿还的债务义务。该部于周日在一份声明中表明了这一立场，声明由财政部长兼经济协调部长泰沃·奥耶德莱通过其X账号分享。该部坚持认为，每一奈拉的借款都符合国家议会根据2026年拨款法和批准的借款计划授权的限额。根据声明，政府借款符合2007年财政责任法和2003年债务管理办公室（设立）法，而该国债务义务的详细信息由债务管理办公室定期公布。“这是改革取得成效的结果，而不是财政困境的迹象，”该部宣布。它还拒绝将六个月的财政快照作为债务可持续性的最终衡量标准，坚持认为全年预测能提供更恰当的评估。“同一份世界银行报告预计尼日利亚2026年全年债务偿付（包括利息和本金）占收入的46%。这才是适当的基准，也是避免得出无效结论的指南，”声明写道
